The Settings app

Finding your way around Settings; every page is in the Settings reference

Open Settings with Super+I, from the Aurora menu, from the Control Center, or by typing a setting's name in Spotlight. The sidebar groups pages like Ubuntu's Settings: connectivity, look and feel, devices and input, security, AI, and the system.

Open a page directly from a terminal or a script:

PageOpen it directly
Networkaurora-settings --page network
Bluetoothaurora-settings --page bluetooth
Displaysaurora-settings --page display
Soundaurora-settings --page sound
Poweraurora-settings --page power
Appearanceaurora-settings --page appearance
Desktop & Dockaurora-settings --page desktop
Desktop Profilesaurora-settings --page profiles
Multitaskingaurora-settings --page multitasking
Notificationsaurora-settings --page notifications
Appsaurora-settings --page apps
Screen Timeaurora-settings --page screentime
Mouse & Touchpadaurora-settings --page mouse
Keyboardaurora-settings --page keyboard
Printersaurora-settings --page printers
Accessibilityaurora-settings --page accessibility
Privacy & Securityaurora-settings --page privacy
App Permissionsaurora-settings --page permissions
Sharingaurora-settings --page sharing
AIaurora-settings --page ai
Usersaurora-settings --page users
Language & Regionaurora-settings --page language
Date & Timeaurora-settings --page datetime
Software Updatesaurora-settings --page updates
Storageaurora-settings --page storage
System Healthaurora-settings --page health
Aboutaurora-settings --page about

Every option of every page is listed in the Settings reference.
